newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukrainian parliament voices concern over Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Ukrainian parliament voices concern over Belarus.

text.p: Ukraine's parliament expressed "deep concern" on Tuesday about rising tension in neighbouring Belarus, where President Alexander Lukashenko is locked in a row with parliament over a planned referendum to extend his powers.
A resolution passed after a brief debate referred to the worsening conflict between different branches of authority in Belarus but avoided singling out one side for blame.
"We are strictly following the norms of non-interference in internal affairs but are also strictly following the norms of parliamentary (conduct)," the resolution said.

"We call on the representatives of executive and legislative authority in this friendly state to display mutual understanding and act exclusively in a constitutional way to maintain democracy and security in the region," it said.
The Ukrainian parliament said it was certain that the "fraternal Belarussian people" would find a constitutional way out of their internal problems.
An initial draft of the resolution blamed Lukashenko for undermining the constitution but a majority of deputies agreed that they should avoid taking sides in the dispute.
Ukrainian nationalist deputies wanted a harder statement, mentioning the position of the 300,000-strong Ukrainian ethnic minority in Belarus.

Ukraine's government, like Russia's, has kept silent on the Belarus conflict but parliamentary speaker Oleksander Moroz said on Monday he was in continuous contact with his Belarussian counterpart Semyon Sharetsky, prominent in the opposition to Lukashenko.
Seven Ukrainian nationalist activists from the far-right Ukrainian National Assembly (UNA) have been in jail in Belarus since April for taking part in anti-Lukashenko protests.
On November 15 the Belarussian Supreme Court dismissed an appeal against their sentences for public order offences.
